namespace ApexGraph

open SimpleGraph

/-- `H` is a minor of `G` if the vertices of `H` can be represented by nonempty, connected,
pairwise disjoint branch sets in `G`, with every edge of `H` represented by an edge between the
corresponding branch sets. -/
def IsMinor {U V : Type*} (H : SimpleGraph U) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ branch : U → Set V,
    (∀ u, (G.induce (branch u)).Connected) ∧
    (∀ ⦃u v⦄, u ≠ v → Disjoint (branch u) (branch v)) ∧
    ∀ ⦃u v⦄, H.Adj u v → ∃ x ∈ branch u, ∃ y ∈ branch v, G.Adj x y

/-- A finite simple graph is planar if it has neither $K_5$ nor $K_{3,3}$ as a minor. This is
Wagner's forbidden-minor characterization of planar graphs. -/
def IsPlanar {V : Type*} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 5)) G ∧
    ¬ IsMinor (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin 3) (Fin 3)) G

/-- A nonempty finite graph is apex if deleting some vertex leaves a planar graph. -/
def IsApex {V : Type*} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ v : V, IsPlanar (G.induce ({v} : Set V)ᶜ)

/--
**Jørgensen's conjecture.** Every $6$-vertex-connected graph with no $K_6$ minor is an apex
graph: it has a vertex whose deletion leaves a planar graph.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem apex_graph :
    ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      IsKConnected G 6 → ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 6)) G → IsApex G := by
  sorry

end ApexGraph

The repository's `SimpleGraph.IsKConnected G 6` is used for 6-vertex-connectivity; it requires more than six vertices and connectivity after deletion of every set of fewer than six vertices.
Graph minors are modeled by pairwise disjoint nonempty connected branch sets, with each edge of the minor represented by an edge between the corresponding branch sets.
For finite simple graphs, planarity is defined using Wagner's equivalent forbidden-minor characterization: neither `K_5` nor `K_{3,3}` is a minor.

Vertex deletion is represented by the induced graph on the complement of a singleton. Apex means that such a vertex exists. Although the background article specially counts the null graph as apex, the conjecture only concerns graphs with more than six vertices, so the existential formulation is exactly equivalent on its domain.

/-!
# Apex graphs and Jørgensen's conjecture

An *apex graph* is a graph that can be made planar by the removal of a single vertex.
Jørgensen (1994) conjectured that every $6$-connected graph with no $K_6$ minor is an apex graph.
The conjecture is open. Kawarabayashi, Norine, Thomas and Wollan proved it for all sufficiently
large graphs, so if it is false then it has only finitely many counterexamples.

Mathlib has neither graph minors nor planarity, so both notions are defined here.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Apex graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/apex_graph)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Jør94] L. K. Jørgensen, *Contractions to $K_8$*, J. Graph Theory 18 (1994), 431–448.
- [KNTW12] K. Kawarabayashi, S. Norine, R. Thomas, P. Wollan, *$K_6$ minors in large 6-connected
  graphs*, [arXiv:1203.2192](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.2192).
-/

namespace ApexGraph

open SimpleGraph
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

variable {V W : Type*}

/-- `IsMinor H G` says that `H` is a minor of `G`, i.e. `H` can be obtained from a subgraph of `G`
by contracting edges. This is stated through a *model* of `H` in `G`: a family of pairwise
disjoint *branch sets* `B w ⊆ V` (one for each vertex `w` of `H`), each inducing a connected (in
particular nonempty) subgraph of `G`, such that for every edge `x ~ y` of `H` some edge of `G` joins
`B x` to `B y`. Deleting the vertices outside the branch sets and contracting each branch set to
a single vertex yields a graph containing a copy of `H`. -/
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ B : W → Set V, Pairwise (fun x y ↦ Disjoint (B x) (B y)) ∧
    (∀ w, (G.induce (B w)).Connected) ∧ ∀ x y, H.Adj x y → ∃ u ∈ B x, ∃ v ∈ B y, G.Adj u v

/-- `IsPlanar G` says that `G` is planar: it has a drawing in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$
without crossings. That is, there are an injective map `f` from the vertices to the plane and, for
each edge `e`, an arc `arc e` (the range of an injective path in the plane) joining the images of
the two ends of `e`, such that no arc passes through the image of a vertex other than its ends,
and two distinct arcs meet only in images of vertices (hence only in their common ends). -/
def IsPlanar (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (f : V → ℝ²) (arc : G.edgeSet → Set ℝ²),
    Function.Injective f ∧
    (∀ e : G.edgeSet, ∃ (u v : V) (γ : Path (f u) (f v)),
      (e : Sym2 V) = s(u, v) ∧ Function.Injective γ ∧ Set.range γ = arc e) ∧
    (∀ (e : G.edgeSet) (w : V), f w ∈ arc e → w ∈ (e : Sym2 V)) ∧
    ∀ e₁ e₂ : G.edgeSet, e₁ ≠ e₂ → arc e₁ ∩ arc e₂ ⊆ Set.range f

/-- `IsApex G` says that `G` is an apex graph: some vertex `v` of `G` can be deleted so that the
remaining graph `G - v` is planar. (Wikipedia also counts the null graph as an apex graph; this
convention plays no role for graphs with at least one vertex.) -/
def IsApex (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ v : V, IsPlanar (G.induce {v}ᶜ)

/-- Every graph is a minor of itself, with branch sets the singletons. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_refl (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsMinor G G := by
  refine ⟨fun w ↦ {w}, ?_, fun w ↦ ?_, fun x y h ↦ ⟨x, rfl, y, rfl, h⟩⟩
  · intro x y hxy
    simpa using hxy
  · haveI : Nonempty ({w} : Set V) := ⟨⟨w, rfl⟩⟩
    exact Connected.of_subsingleton

/-- A finite graph without edges is planar. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isPlanar_bot (n : ℕ) : IsPlanar (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) := by
  have h : IsEmpty (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet := by
    simp [edgeSet_bot]
  refine ⟨fun i ↦ EuclideanSpace.single 0 (i : ℝ), fun e ↦ h.elim e, ?_, fun e ↦ h.elim e,
    fun e ↦ h.elim e, fun e ↦ h.elim e⟩
  intro i j hij
  have := congrFun (congrArg (⇑) hij) 0
  simp at this
  exact Fin.ext (by exact_mod_cast this)

/-- **Jørgensen's conjecture.** Every $6$-vertex-connected graph with no $K_6$ minor is an apex
graph, i.e. it has a vertex whose deletion leaves a planar graph.

Here a finite graph is $6$-connected (`IsKConnected G 6`) if it has more than $6$ vertices and
remains connected after the deletion of any set of fewer than $6$ vertices. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem apex_graph [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : G.IsKConnected 6)
    (hK₆ : ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 6)) G) : IsApex G := by
  sorry

end ApexGraph

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Apex graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/apex_graph)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in

* [KNTW12] Kawarabayashi, K., Norine, S., Thomas, R., Wollan, P. (2012).
  "$K_6$ minors in large 6-connected graphs". [arXiv:1203.2192](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.2192)
-/

open Function SimpleGraph
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace ApexGraph

variable {V W : Type*}

/-- `IsMinor H G` says that `H` is a minor of `G`. It is defined by branch sets: a family `B`
of pairwise disjoint vertex sets of `G`, indexed by the vertices of `H`, such that every `B x`
induces a connected (hence nonempty) subgraph of `G` and, for every edge `xy` of `H`, some edge
of `G` joins `B x` to `B y`. Contracting each branch set to a single vertex and deleting all
other vertices and edges of `G` gives a graph containing a copy of `H`. This is the standard
description of a graph minor for simple graphs. -/
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ B : W → Set V, Pairwise (Disjoint on B) ∧ (∀ x, (G.induce (B x)).Connected) ∧
    ∀ x y, H.Adj x y → ∃ u ∈ B x, ∃ v ∈ B y, G.Adj u v

/-- `IsPlanarEmbedding G f arc` says that `f` and `arc` form a planar embedding (a drawing
without crossings) of `G` in the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$:
* the vertices are placed at the pairwise distinct points `f v`;
* every edge `e` is drawn as the Jordan arc `arc e`, the range of an injective path between the
  images of its two endpoints;
* an arc contains the image of a vertex only if that vertex is an endpoint of the edge;
* two distinct arcs meet only in images of vertices, hence only in common endpoints. -/
structure IsPlanarEmbedding (G : SimpleGraph V) (f : V → ℝ²) (arc : G.edgeSet → Set ℝ²) :
    Prop where
  injective : Injective f
  exists_path (e : G.edgeSet) : ∃ u v, (e : Sym2 V) = s(u, v) ∧
    ∃ γ : _root_.Path (f u) (f v), Injective γ ∧ Set.range γ = arc e
  mem_of_mem_arc (e : G.edgeSet) (v : V) : f v ∈ arc e → v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)
  mem_range_of_mem_inter (e e' : G.edgeSet) :
    e ≠ e' → ∀ p ∈ arc e ∩ arc e', p ∈ Set.range f

/-- A graph is planar if it has a planar embedding. -/
def IsPlanar (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (f : V → ℝ²) (arc : G.edgeSet → Set ℝ²), IsPlanarEmbedding G f arc

/-- Every graph is a minor of itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsMinor.refl (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsMinor G G :=
  ⟨fun x => {x}, fun _ _ hne => Set.disjoint_singleton.mpr hne,
    fun _ => Connected.of_subsingleton, fun x y h => ⟨x, rfl, y, rfl, h⟩⟩

/-- A minor of `G` has at most as many vertices as `G`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsMinor.card_le [Fintype V] [Fintype W] {H : SimpleGraph W} {G : SimpleGraph V}
    (h : IsMinor H G) : Fintype.card W ≤ Fintype.card V := by
  obtain ⟨B, hdisj, hconn, -⟩ := h
  refine Fintype.card_le_of_injective (fun x => ((hconn x).nonempty.some : V)) fun x y hxy => ?_
  by_contra hne
  exact (hdisj hne).ne_of_mem (hconn x).nonempty.some.2 (hconn y).nonempty.some.2 hxy

/-- A graph with fewer than `6` vertices has no `K₆` minor. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isMinor_completeGraph_six [Fintype V] {G : SimpleGraph V} (hV : Fintype.card V < 6) :
    ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 6)) G := fun h => by
  have := h.card_le
  simp only [Fintype.card_fin] at this
  omega

/-- A graph with at most one vertex is planar. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isPlanar_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton V] (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsPlanar G := by
  have hedge : ∀ e : G.edgeSet, False := fun ⟨e, he⟩ =>
    Sym2.ind (fun u v huv => G.ne_of_adj huv (Subsingleton.elim u v)) e he
  exact ⟨fun _ => 0, fun e => (hedge e).elim,
    fun a b _ => Subsingleton.elim a b, fun e => (hedge e).elim, fun e => (hedge e).elim,
    fun e => (hedge e).elim⟩

/-- **Jørgensen's conjecture** (1994). Every $6$-vertex-connected graph with no $K_6$ minor is
an apex graph: it has a vertex whose deletion leaves a planar graph.

Graphs are finite and simple. `G.IsKConnected 6` means that `G` has more than `6` vertices and
stays connected after the deletion of any set of fewer than `6` vertices. In particular `G` has
a vertex, so the conclusion agrees with every convention on apex graphs (the null graph never
satisfies the hypotheses). -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem apex_graph [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (hconn : G.IsKConnected 6)
    (hK₆ : ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 6)) G) :
    ∃ v : V, IsPlanar (G.induce {v}ᶜ) := by

    fun u v h ↦ ⟨_, rfl, _, rfl, by simpa using h⟩⟩

namespace ApexGraph

open SimpleGraph

/--
A simple graph `H` is a minor of `G` if the vertices of `H` can be represented by pairwise
disjoint connected branch sets in `G`, with an edge between the branch sets for every edge of
`H`.
-/
def IsGraphMinor {W V : Type*} (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ branch : W → Set V,
    (∀ w, (G.induce (branch w)).Connected) ∧
    (∀ ⦃x y⦄, x ≠ y → Disjoint (branch x) (branch y)) ∧
    (∀ ⦃x y⦄, H.Adj x y → ∃ u ∈ branch x, ∃ v ∈ branch y, G.Adj u v)

/--
A graph is planar if it has neither $K_5$ nor $K_{3,3}$ as a minor, using Wagner's
characterization of planar graphs.
-/
def IsPlanar {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ¬ IsGraphMinor (completeGraph (Fin 5)) G ∧
    ¬ IsGraphMinor (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin 3) (Fin 3)) G

/--
A graph is apex if it is planar, or deleting some vertex leaves a planar graph. The first
alternative includes the null graph, in accordance with the convention in the cited article.
-/
def IsApex {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  IsPlanar G ∨ ∃ apex : V, IsPlanar (G.induce {v | v ≠ apex})

**Jørgensen's conjecture.** Every $6$-vertex-connected graph with no $K_6$ minor is an
apex graph.
-/

    (h_connected : IsKConnected G 6)
    (h_minor_free : ¬ IsGraphMinor (completeGraph (Fin 6)) G) : IsApex G := by
